summary: SL-112 added one size-check watermark to ScanStore, written once as the first statement of Scanner.Run.Finish. Three allocation-free reads derive from it: SizeCheckPending, Unfinished and AtLeast. It also added a StoppedInSizeChecks flag on the final snapshot, a third arm of MainWindow.ListHeader, and a reworded listing-Stop header. It shipped with the suite at 1096 of 1096, no existing test edited, a 5M store retained at 637 MiB and peaking at 653.5 MiB, and sweeps on real temp trees plus System32 and ProgramData with 0 mismatches. Nothing outside the store calls the new reads yet, so the person-visible change is two header sentences. The App payoff waits on SC-393.

payload.estimate_error: Size 'medium' held: 18 files, 8 new tests, 1 fitness rule with 2 plants and 1 window case. Risk 'medium' was a bit high for Core, where the change is a read with no callers and an O(1) write. It was fair for the surrounding work: three decided header questions, the rules harness, and WindowMutants (382-398 s). The reruns do not measure difficulty. Design-slice ran twice and critique twice because each halted for a person or model answer. Build ran three times because the provider refused two attempts (session limit, then OAuth refresh), and attempt 1 had already left working code. The only slice-caused rework was folding Q-283 into the listing header and moving the 'sized from the file' predicate out of ScanStore. Critique-review did not run, by sizing. That left critique and code review as the only model gates, and between them they caught everything the build and validation then confirmed.

learned.lesson: When a design halts on an open question and the question is answered later, design-slice's 'accept' path re-passed the old design unchanged. The answer then reached the loop as a major critique finding. Next time, hand the answered question to the critique brief explicitly, or re-synthesise the design before accepting it.
learned.evidence: design-slice #1 halted on the listing-Stop header question. design-slice #2 'Accept the SL-112 attempt 1 design' kept the header byte-identical. Critique M1 (major) then found it contradicted Q-283, forcing the listing arm, the L-001 literal and $StoppedListHeader to be reworked.

learned.lesson: Treat Q-111, Q-160 and Q-283 as superseded wherever they quote header text. Two model-decided answers were wrong against this slice's own measurement. Q-160 assumed Done-row file sizes are complete. Q-283 kept 'Rows marked ... are short'. A stale-large hardlink first name makes a Done row or a marked row sit above final. The shipped strings now say 'may be off' and drop 'are short'. The source of truth is $StoppedListHeader and $StoppedSizingHeader in tests/window/WindowCases.ps1, not the question text.
learned.evidence: Survey run A: 3-shrink stopped at (64 MiB, 64 MiB, 1) against final (1 MiB, 1 MiB, 1). At-least spike: the un-subtracted listed figure exceeded the reference in 20,998 unfinished folders. Build deviations 2 and 5; L-001 and L-004 pass with the new strings.

learned.lesson: A fitness rule constrains both directions of a dependency. Putting the shared 'sized from the file' predicate on ScanStore and calling it from SizeProbe satisfied 'the store does not know the Scanner'. It broke 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore before the scan ends'. The predicate now lives in the neutral internal class Store/EntryRules.cs. Any further predicate shared by Scanning and Store goes there, and a design should check both rules before choosing a home.
learned.evidence: The rules harness clean baseline was not clean on its first run: the rule fired at SizeProbe.cs:28. Fixed with EntryRules; the harness then read 169/169 with 0 stray hits and a clean 100-rule baseline.

learned.lesson: SizeCheckPending, Unfinished, AtLeast and NotListedAtOrBelow have no caller in src outside ScanStore, so a green suite is not App coverage. SC-393 is the first consumer. It must guard Count 0 first, and call the reads only after Scan has returned. Mid-scan the watermark is 0, so Unfinished over-marks everything and AtLeast subtracts every file's listing size. A pause in the sizing pass (U-180/U-197) is only safe after SC-407's advancing cursor, or after a per-range structure with a 5M memory test.
learned.evidence: Design contract on Unfinished ('on the writing thread before then it over-marks (watermark 0)'). Code-review drift item 4. EndSizeChecks is written once, in Finish. Design obligation recorded in docs/design/SL-112-unfinished-at-stop.md.

learned.lesson: The stale-hardlink fixtures only work with one recipe: write the stale length through the first name, then change the file through a later name, and re-stale before EVERY scan, references included. A probe open refreshes the stale entry. Without the recipe this NTFS lists true sizes (U-130 saw zero staleness), so the sweep goes void. UnfinishedTests re-stales with SetLength, not mklink per scan, and fails on a ProbeCorrections floor rather than passing. Real trees gave no stale hardlink first name and no downward correction, so AtLeast's subtraction is exercised only on engineered trees.
learned.evidence: Spike: 12/12 first names stale with the recipe, 0 void in 1,540 scans. Validate: System32 and ProgramData gave rolledAboveRef 0. Review M2 and O-017: Restale via SetLength, no process spawned.

learned.lesson: A numeric time bound prescribed in a critique should be tested by mutating the thing it guards. M2 prescribed 25 s per row. The builder's mklink-per-scan mutant still passed at 24 s. Only a 15 s bound asserted at every Stop failed it, at 16.9 s. Core Facts here take 0.7-2.6 s and case commands 5.6-13.1 s. The cases near the engine's 120 s kill (Q-222) are the window ones: L-001 took 38 s with a publish, L-004 took 30 s.
learned.evidence: Build account: mutation 'Restale re-makes the link with TempHardlink before every scan' failed with 'past the 15 s bound set for one case command (71 stops so far)'. At 25 s it passed at 24 s. The bound was tightened to 15 s.

learned.lesson: Criterion 5 ('nothing more is written once Stop has taken effect') is MET only for the wind-down window. NothingChangesOnceTheScanHasReturned looks while the stuck workers finish. A watermark rewrite 30 ms after return turns it red; one 300 ms after return does not. Nothing seals the store. Do not cite criterion 5 as proof against a late writer such as a resume path, until SC-408 and SC-411 land.
learned.evidence: Validate mutation for O-001: Delay(30) red with 625 entries differing; Delay(300) survived. O-019 waived to SC-408; SC-411 filed.

learned.lesson: Verification cost dominates a slice that edits fitness.yaml and src/FsAnalyser.App. The harness, RuleCases C-001/C-003 and WindowMutants -Mutant All each ran in build and again in validate (suite 50 s, WindowMutants 382-398 s). Lesson #486's 'three or more runs' held. Budget a slice like this by its verification runs, not by its Core diff.
learned.evidence: Build and validate both ran WindowMutants (398 s and 382 s) and the rules harness (169/169). The Core diff is one int, three reads and one Finish block.

learned.lesson: Code review found three departures the builder did not declare: StopTree group H and a void floor of 7 instead of 8; the listing sweep stopping through Scans.RunCancellingAt instead of NotListedTests.StopAt (lesson #511); and a doc comment overstating the 4-worker stuck row. When a design names a helper by lesson number, the build's declared-deviations list should say whether the helper was used.
learned.evidence: Code-review LEFT OPEN drift items 1-3. The builder's own deviation list covered EntryRules, the header wording, Tally.Bound and the BOM only.

lessons_judged.why: A Done row is not final, so AtLeast is a separate read and the headers say 'may be off'. The Facts compare only non-Unfinished folders with the reference.
AtLeast subtracts only files that charge (ChecksOwnSize), and the sweeps compare charged figures by path.
Scanner.cs gained a comment at the FolderDone push loop and the design record cross-references SL-111. A page-straddling 70,000-child synthetic store covers the gap the lesson named.
EndSizeChecks accepts 0 at Count 0, and the listing sweep includes calls 1-2, which gave 4 empty stores.

The 'first name is the same entry' precondition rests on single-threaded, deterministic order. The design record names it as an obligation for any slice that parallelises, and the sweep asserts the charged name equals the reference's.
'Stop has taken effect' was defined as Scanner.Scan returning, on the grounds that the store is frozen after that.
The stopped tree header was left unchanged and filed to SC-393. No stopped-tree memory measurement was taken.
No cancel-safety is claimed, and the network pass is listed as a person-run debt in the build and validation.
L-004 roots under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp with a per-run GUID and [IO.Directory]::Delete. The orphan sweep was waived to SC-409.
No new opt-in test Trait was added.
Every build, test and publish went through eng/dotnet.ps1.
The ragged fixture was used. Code review noted the listing sweep stopped through RunCancellingAt rather than StopAt; Baseline and the stops share Options(), so the call numbers still line up.
New raw Kind reads were spelled == (byte)EntryKind.X inside the grammar, and KindByteWriteCorpusTests stayed green and unedited.
The baseline of 637.1 MiB retained and 653.6 MiB peak against 800 MiB was reproduced (637.3 and 653.7). The reads left retained memory within 1 MiB and allocated 0 bytes.
The EndSizeChecks rule went in as a settled entry with plant rows S87 (fire) and P37 (quiet). The harness read 169/169.
The rules harness and RuleCases C-001/C-003 were budgeted for build and validate. The rule is a tripwire for one spelling, and the design record says it does not close the class.
dotnet test does not run window cases, so L-004 was added and L-001 and L-004 were run explicitly with a fresh publish.
The hook trigger FSA_HOOK_AT_SIZED existed and was read directly. No critique claim about hook modes or lifecycle needed overriding.
Nobody consulted it. The footprint (18 files, 8 tests against a design of '6 Facts and Theories') matches its warning, but size held at medium.

what_went_wrong: The design halted on an open question about the listing-Stop header. Q-283 answered it afterwards. design-slice #2 then accepted the attempt-1 design unchanged, with the header byte-identical. Critique M1 (major) found the contradiction, and the listing arm, L-001, $StoppedListHeader and a WindowMutants run had to be redone.

The design put ChecksOwnSize on ScanStore with SizeProbe calling it, and its coherence check said the fitness rules stayed unbroken. 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore before the scan ends' fired at SizeProbe.cs:28, and the rules harness's clean baseline was not clean. The build created EntryRules.cs to fix it.

Build ran three times. Two attempts were refused by the provider (session limit, then OAuth refresh), and the third had to review attempt 1's leftover code before keeping it. This cost time but is not a design fault.
The per-row time bound the critique prescribed (25 s, from M2) was too loose. The mklink-per-scan mutant passed at 24 s, and the builder only found this by mutating. The shipped bound is 15 s.

Two model-decided header answers (Q-160 and Q-283) contradicted the slice's own measurements. The shipped headers depart from Q-111, Q-160 and Q-283 by dropping 'are short' and using 'may be off'. The builder declared this, and Q-283 says to revert if the owner wanted its literal wording.

Code review found three undeclared departures: StopTree group H with a void floor of 7 instead of 8; the listing sweep stopping through RunCancellingAt instead of StopAt; and an overstated '4-worker row' comment. None changed behaviour.

Validate's mutation showed NothingChangesOnceTheScanHasReturned misses a watermark rewrite 300 ms after Scan returns. Review m3 had predicted this and it was waived to SC-408. Criterion 5 therefore rests on a window shorter than 'while the stopped results are open'.
All 11 critique findings were dispositioned by a model, not a person, so they count as untriaged in that gate's precision. No gate between critique and code review checked those dispositions.

missed.what: The design placed ChecksOwnSize on ScanStore with SizeProbe.IsEligible calling it. Its coherence check named only the rule 'the store does not know about the Scanner'. It did not check the opposite direction. The fitness rule 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore before the scan ends' fires on SizeProbe.cs referencing ScanStore. The critique listed the neutral class as taste and never grepped the Scanning to Store direction against .taad/fitness.yaml.
missed.caught_by: build: the rules harness clean baseline was not clean on its first run (SizeProbe.cs:28), which led to EntryRules.cs

missed.what: Finding M2 prescribed 'about 25 s per row' without checking that the bound had teeth. The builder's mklink-per-scan mutant still passed at 24 s. A bound is only useful if it fails the slow variant it guards against. The critique did not ask what the slowest wrong implementation would score.
missed.caught_by: build: a hand mutation of Restale, which led to the 15 s per-Stop Tally.Bound

missed.what: The code review ran four mutations on the store reads and the cutoff. It ran none that writes the store after Scan returns, so NothingChangesOnceTheScanHasReturned went uninterrogated. It survives a watermark rewrite 300 ms after return, and its doc comment says 'every probe worker stuck' when StuckStop blocks one call. Criterion 5's test was reviewed by reading only.
missed.caught_by: validate: the Delay(30) mutation turned the test red and the Delay(300) mutation survived, which showed the test's blind window

unknowns: On a real drive, how often does AtLeast's subtraction differ from the rolled figure? System32, ProgramData and Program Files gave no stale hardlink first name and no downward correction (rolledAboveRef 0). Only engineered trees, and the OneDrive and LZNT1 first-scan cases, show the effect.

Does SC-393's per-row AtLeast keep the 100k-child folder open under 0.5 s on a real ~1M-folder C:\? The synthetic 4.88M-entry store gave 29 ms and 6 ms for 100k rows, and 18-25 ms in the spike when every child is a folder. Q-280 is still open.

Does UnfinishedTests stay green on Windows 10 or on a build where NTFS does not list stale hardlink names? It fails as void on its ProbeCorrections floor and is never skipped. It was only run on Win11 26200.

Will a Pause (U-180/U-197) ever land in the sizing pass? If so, the one-int watermark will not describe it, because mid-scan it reads 0 and applied batches are not recorded. SC-407 or a per-range structure is needed first.
Did the owner want Q-111's and Q-283's header wording word for word? Q-283 says to revert if so, and the build dropped 'are short' on measurement grounds.

candidates.title: Supersede the header wording in Q-111, Q-160 and Q-283 with the shipped strings, and get the owner to confirm the dropped 'are short' clause
candidates.why: The listing-Stop header in MainWindow.ListHeader (final, non-sizing arm) and the sizing arm shipped at 172ab8b without 'are short', which departs from three decided questions. Q-283 reads DECIDED and says 'revert if the owner wanted the Q-111 wording'. Survey run A (3-shrink 64 MiB against 1 MiB final) and the at-least sweep (20,998 unfinished folders above the reference) contradict 'are short'. SC-393 will wire at-least figures and may revisit the header. If it reads Q-283 as authoritative it will rebuild the contradicted sentence. The current strings are $StoppedListHeader and $StoppedSizingHeader in tests/window/WindowCases.ps1.

candidates.title: Add a standing WindowMutants mutant for the sizing-Stop header arm (L-004 / StoppedInSizeChecks)
candidates.why: The build proved only the listing arm by hand: it reverted the arm in MainWindow.xaml.cs and L-001 went red. No account records a mutant for the new third arm. WindowMutants -Mutant All ran 12 mutants at 398 s in build and 382 s in validate. The flag Cancelled && _uncheckedFrom > 0 in Scanner.Run.Finish, and the arm it selects, are guarded by L-004 (30 s) and by Core Facts, but not by a roster entry. Check tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1's ValidateSet for an existing one before building.

filed.title: Check by hand: Whether the OneDrive sync folder (inside %USERPROFILE%) and whole C:\ also give zero unchanged single-link negatives on a second scan
The watermark is recorded only on one exit.
The design's one must-verify precondition, 'nothing writes the store after Scanner.Scan returns, including the watermark', is held by remembering.
Mutation for O-001: store watermark rewritten 300 ms after Scan returns
